newsitem.title: UK: UK insurers face competition in underwriting.
newsitem.headline: UK insurers face competition in underwriting.

text.p: Banks, building societies and brokers are moving into the traditional underwriting preserve of UK insurers, who stand to lose 20 percent of their household business, management consultancy Datamonitor said on Monday.

"The biggest shake up will be in personal property insurance where banks and building societies will set up their own direct underwriting operations," Datamonitor said in its 'UK Personal General Insurance' report.
Personal motor business will also be snapped up as intermediaries, who traditionally supplied insurers with business, opt to underwrite the risks themselves.

Banks, building societies and brokers have been pushed in this direction by the emergence of direct telephone insurers, who have taken away much of their business in the past decade, Datamonitor said.
They are now well placed to compete with direct insurers, particularly in property insurance, where telephone insurers have made less of an inroad than motor.

"Brokers such as AA and Swinton, and building societies such as the Halifax already have well established customer bases and the resources to invest in the kind of systems that have allowed the tele-underwriters to gain share so quickly,"

"These category killers have the potential to become the major players in the tele-sales of property insurance, putting a halt to the rapid growth of direct writers as well as starving the composites of business."
